C1: (1) Humanoid:MoveTo has a built-in ~8 s timeout: if the goal isn't reached in ~8 s the walk stops and MoveToFinished fires with reached=false. Your code ignores the boolean, so it prints 'arrived' anyway. (2) MoveTo walks in a straight line; it never avoids obstacles. Fix: use PathfindingService. local path = PathfindingService:CreatePath({AgentRadius=2, AgentCanJump=true}); pcall(path.ComputeAsync, path, root.Position, target.Position); check path.Status == Enum.PathStatus.Success; then for each waypoint: if wp.Action == Enum.PathWaypointAction.Jump then hum.Jump = true end; hum:MoveTo(wp.Position); local ok = hum.MoveToFinished:Wait(); if not ok then recompute end. Each short waypoint MoveTo resets the 8 s timer. Connect path.Blocked(idx) to recompute when a blocked waypoint is ahead, and repath every 0.5-1 s for a moving target. Also call root:SetNetworkOwner(nil) so the server drives the NPC without client-ownership stutter.
C2: ScreenGui.ResetOnSpawn defaults to true: on every respawn the PlayerGui copy is destroyed and re-cloned from StarterGui, so the LocalScript re-runs from scratch and its local variables reset. Fix: set ResetOnSpawn = false on the settings ScreenGui (the script then runs once and state persists), or keep settings outside the GUI (a ModuleScript/client state in PlayerScripts or attributes on the Player) and re-apply on spawn. To persist across sessions, send the settings to the server (validated) and save them in a DataStore.
C3: Animations replicate only when played through an Animator the network model knows about. Your own character: the client owns it and the Animator is created by the server (Humanoid), so client-played animations on your own character replicate to everyone. The server-owned NPC: a client playing tracks on a server-owned Humanoid/Animator is local-only; it doesn't replicate. The NPC whose Animator you created with Instance.new on the client: that Animator exists only on your client, so nothing replicates. Fix: play NPC animations from a server Script (Animator created on the server, e.g. Humanoid's default or server-side Instance.new), triggered via a validated RemoteEvent if a client action starts it, or deliberately play them on every client (FireAllClients) if purely cosmetic. Always load via Animator:LoadAnimation, never Humanoid:LoadAnimation, and only create Animators on the server.
C4: (1) A Sound is positional (3D) only when parented to a BasePart or Attachment. Parented directly to Workspace (or SoundService) it is global, same volume for everyone. Fix: parent it to a part/Attachment at the barrel, with sensible RollOffMinDistance (~20-40) and RollOffMaxDistance (~300-600). (2) Audibility range is governed by RollOffMinDistance (full volume radius, default 10), RollOffMaxDistance (default 10000) and RollOffMode (Inverse default falls off fast). Raise RollOffMinDistance, set RollOffMaxDistance to the range wanted, and use Linear/InverseTapered for a gentle, predictable falloff (InverseTapered avoids the cliff). (3) Loaded fires once; if the sound already loaded before you connected, Wait() never returns, and if the asset is moderated/removed it never loads. Fix: if not siren.IsLoaded then waitWithTimeout(siren.Loaded, 5) end, then play; or just call :Play() (it plays when ready) / use ContentProvider:PreloadAsync.

workspace:Raycast(origin, direction) uses the direction vector's LENGTH as the ray distance. .Unit has length 1, so the ray is only 1 stud long and almost always returns nil; then result.Instance errors. And starting from the head, the 1-stud ray hits your own character. Fix:
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {player.Character}
local dir = (mouseHit - head.Position).Unit * 500
local result = workspace:Raycast(head.Position, dir, params)
if result then print(result.Instance.Name) end
Always nil-check results. For a real gun, do the authoritative raycast on the server (validate origin/direction/rate) and only use the client cast for effects.
C6: Two tweens on the same property of the same instance conflict: playing the second cancels the first (TweenService overrides the earlier tween), so the hover tween is cut off at whatever value it reached and the click flash's 'back' target was computed from that midway value. Structure: keep one controller per button with a single source of truth (state: idle/hover/pressed), store the current tween, Cancel() it before starting a new one, and always tween to the target for the current state (hover target 0.2, idle target base value), never to a value captured mid-tween. Let the click flash end by returning to the state's target (if still hovered -> 0.2). Better still, animate different properties for different effects (e.g. flash with a UIStroke/overlay frame or UIScale while hover owns BackgroundTransparency) so they never fight. Debounce clicks.

local store = game:GetService('DataStoreService'):GetDataStore('PlayerData')
local function addGems(userId: number, amount: number): (boolean, number?)
  local key = 'Player_' .. userId
  for attempt = 1, 3 do
    local ok, result = pcall(function()
      return store:UpdateAsync(key, function(old)
        local data = old or {Gems = 0}
        data.Gems = (data.Gems or 0) + amount
        return data
      end)
    end)
    if ok then return true, result.Gems end
    warn('addGems failed', attempt, result)
    task.wait(2 ^ attempt)
  end
  return false
end
Callback rules: it must be fast and non-yielding (no waits, no other DataStore calls), have no side effects (it may run several times on retries/conflicts), derive the new value only from 'old' (handle nil for new players), return nil to cancel the write, and return only serializable data under 4 MB. Error handling: wrap in pcall, retry with backoff for transient errors, respect request budgets (GetRequestBudgetForRequestType), and validate amount server-side. Don't use GetAsync+SetAsync for increments (race).

C13: Use MemoryStoreService (a MemoryStoreSortedMap keyed by skill/time, or a MemoryStoreQueue) - in-memory, low-latency, shared across all servers, with expirations. DataStores are too slow, rate-limited and durable (not meant for transient, high-churn data). Limits: memory quota 64 KB + 1.2 KB x users (shrinks only after an 8-day look-back); requests 1,000 + 120 x CCU units/min experience-wide (ReadAsync costs items returned plus wait time; UpdateAsync >= 2 units); ~32 KB per item; max expiration 3,888,000 s (45 days); per-partition throughput limits (spread across several maps/keys). Errors: TotalMemoryOverLimit, TotalRequestsOverLimit, PartitionRequestsOverLimit. Design: give entries short TTLs (minutes) and refresh heartbeats; Queue ReadAsync makes items invisible for the invisibility timeout (default 30 s) - call RemoveAsync after processing or they reappear and get matched twice; use one matchmaker (elected via a lock key with UpdateAsync) to avoid double-grouping; pcall + backoff everything; keep only IDs/skill in the store; widen skill range over wait time; teleport groups with ReserveServerAsync; anything that must persist goes to DataStore.

UnreliableRemoteEvent rules: no delivery guarantee and no ordering (packets can drop or arrive out of order), payloads over ~1,000 bytes are dropped, excess over the throttle is dropped rather than queued, and if there is no handler connected the event is discarded. So send compact, self-contained snapshots (latest state + timestamp/sequence number, ignore older ones), at a modest rate (10-20 Hz), and interpolate on the client. Keep lap completion, race results, and any state change (e.g. 'effect stop', item pickups) on a reliable RemoteEvent (ordered, guaranteed) or attributes - a dropped 'stop' would leave effects stuck. Note cars are usually driver-network-owned, so physics positions already replicate; you mainly need inputs/cosmetics. Server still validates anything gameplay-relevant.
C18: Unanchored parts are simulated by an owner; with automatic network ownership the server hands the boss to the nearest player when they come close, so ownership flips between server and clients -> stutter/teleporting, and the owning client can move the boss or fake physics/Touched events. Fix: on the server call boss.HumanoidRootPart:SetNetworkOwner(nil) (after parenting, for every unanchored part assembly) so the server always simulates it; re-assert it if parts are rebuilt. Damage: don't rely on Touched (fires from the owner's simulation and can be spoofed/unreliable); do server-side hit detection - spatial queries (GetPartBoundsInBox/Radius or raycasts) from the boss's attack at the attack moment, with cooldowns and distance checks. Client effects can be cosmetic only.
C19: Put turret logic under Actors: e.g. split 60 turrets across several Actors (a few per core, e.g. 4-8 Actors, each with a Script handling its turrets) rather than one script. In each script: RunService.Heartbeat:ConnectParallel(function() ... end) (or task.desynchronize()). In the parallel phase, read positions/attributes and call workspace:Raycast / Blockcast / GetPartBoundsInBox (thread-safe reads), and compute results into local tables. Then task.synchronize() and apply writes (rotate turrets, fire, set properties, fire remotes) in the serial phase. Restrictions: most property writes, creating/parenting/destroying instances, and many APIs are not allowed in parallel (check each member's thread-safety tag) - writes error until you synchronize. Each Actor has its own Lua VM: module state is not shared (require gives a separate copy), so share data via Actor messages (SendMessage/BindToMessage, args are copied), attributes, or SharedTable (SharedTable.increment is atomic; SharedTable.update may run multiple times, keep it pure). Also reduce work first: profile with MicroProfiler, raycast at lower rates, skip turrets with no nearby targets.

The Input Action System is a declarative, cross-device input layer: InputContext (a group of actions you enable/disable and prioritise, e.g. 'OnFoot', 'Vehicle', 'Menu') -> InputAction children (named actions with a Type: Bool, Direction1D/2D/3D, ViewportPosition) -> InputBinding children (KeyCode e.g. LeftShift / ButtonL3, modifiers, UI button for touch, Scale). Give each action keyboard, gamepad and touch bindings. Reading Sprint (LocalScript):

sprint.Pressed:Connect(function() hum.WalkSpeed = 24 end)
sprint.Released:Connect(function() hum.WalkSpeed = 16 end)
-- or poll: if sprint:GetState() then ... end
Enable via ctx.Enabled = true; use Priority/Sink to resolve conflicts. 2026: Roblox announced (June 2026) that the default PlayerModule/control scripts are being rebuilt on the Input Action System, controlled by StarterPlayer.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem: opt-in from June 2026 (default Disabled), planned default Enabled early 2027 and the property removed mid-2027. Things that may break: require(PlayerModule):GetControls() hacks, reliance on old input sinking/ContextActionService ordering, and forked player scripts. Test with it enabled now.
